subject: Data routing minimization & subprocessor activation schedule
messages:
From: Rebecca Liu <dpo@helioshealth.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data routing minimization and subprocessor activation timeline

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the work so far on the DPA addendum. A few follow-ups from our side as we prep for procurement:

1) Region pinning: Helios needs an explicit statement of how Redwood will minimize cross-border processing for PHI-derived requests. We understand temporary failover for capacity is necessary, but we need bounds (time, scope, and notification).

2) Subprocessor activation: please confirm how much lead time Helios will receive before a new subprocessor begins processing Helios traffic. We need both the standard onboarding window and the emergency/auto-scale activation path (if any).

3) Data minimization during transit: when cross-region bursts occur, what telemetry/metrics are sent cross-border and for how long are logs retained outside the pin region?

Can you share your proposed commitments and any supporting artifacts (subprocessor roster, activation runbook)? Attaching our current SLA redlines for context (Helios_DPO_SLA_redline_v2.docx).

Appreciate a short summary and a call if useful — procurement is aiming to close the week of May 25.

Best,
Rebecca Liu
DPO, Helios Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Liu <dpo@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@helioshealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Data routing minimization and subprocessor activation timeline

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the redlines. Short answer up front: we can commit to region pinning with bounded transient failover and a defined subprocessor activation notice for standard onboarding; we propose a shorter emergency activation path with post-notification and auditability. Details and attachments below.

Summary of proposed commitments (high level):
- Region pinning: Primary processing will occur in Helios-designated region (US-East). Requests will be routed to pinned region by default.
- Transient failover: In rare capacity or regional outage events, we allow cross-region processing for a bounded window of up to 36 hours for active requests and autoscaling (we choose 36 hours to balance safety and operational realities). We will notify Helios within 2 hours of the start of any transient cross-region processing, and provide a written incident summary within 72 hours after normal routing resumes.
- Subprocessor activation: Standard onboarding notification = 10 business days before Helios traffic is routed to a newly onboarded subprocessor. Emergency/auto-scale activation (e.g., burst capacity) can occur with 48 hours notice where technically possible; when we cannot give prior notice (urgent failover), we will notify within 4 hours and provide full activation logs within 3 business days.
- Telemetry & logs: Cross-region telemetry is minimized to service-level metrics required for routing and capacity (no payload-level telemetry). Cross-region audit logs are retained for up to 30 days outside the pinned region for troubleshooting; we will mirror critical audit trails back to the pinned region within 7 days.

Attachments I'm sharing: subprocessor_roster.csv (current roster), transient-egress-playbook.pdf (ops runbook for cross-region events), proposed-dpa-addendum.docx (redlines aligned to commitments above).

Open questions for Helios: do you require in-region KMS for customer keys, and do you need logs to be stored exclusively in-region for >30 days? If so we can propose an escrowed-key setup but that moves this to an enterprise addendum.

Next steps: happy to hop on a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the playbook and answer any legal/process questions. If Helios is happy with these commitments I can circulate a short addendum we can both sign.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Data routing minimization and subprocessor activation timeline

Hi Rebecca — thanks again. Per internal review we've tightened the language slightly and attached the artifacts you asked for. Short commitments below and attachments included.

Committed points (final):
- Region pinning: Redwood will route and process Helios requests in US-East by default.
- Bounded transient failover: Cross-region processing for active workloads is limited to a 36-hour window unless Helios provides written approval for an extended window. We will send an initial notification within 2 hours of the start of any cross-region event and a post-incident summary within 72 hours after normal routing resumes.
- Subprocessor activation: Standard notice is 15 business days in the DPA; operational policy is to provide 10 business days where possible. Emergency/auto-scale activation can be triggered with 48 hours notice where possible; if prior notice cannot be given we will notify within 4 hours and deliver activation logs and a timeline within 3 business days.
- Telemetry & logs: Payload-level telemetry will not be routed cross-region. Service-level metrics required for routing may be processed cross-region transiently and associated cross-region logs will be retained for up to 30 days outside the pinned region; critical audit logs will be mirrored to the pinned region within 7 days.

Attachments (stubs in this thread):
- subprocessor_roster.csv — current roster and country of processing per subprocessor
- transient-egress-playbook.pdf — ops steps, notification templates, and escalation matrix
- proposed-dpa-addendum.docx — DPA language including the 15 business day notice and failover clause

Action items:
- Rebecca / Legal: review the attached proposed-dpa-addendum.docx and confirm if in-region KMS is a hard requirement for Helios. If so, we'll propose an enterprise key escrow flow and provide pricing/ops notes.
- Ben/Marissa/Kimberly: if Helios signs off on the above, we should sync with Sales to finalize procurement timeline (Helios was aiming for the week of May 25).

If it's helpful I can schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday morning PT to walk through the playbook and answer questions.

Best,
